stories.name: Costco vs Walmart
stories.blurb: A series of comparisons weighing whether Costco or Walmart is the better retail stock to buy.

stories.name: Grocery Price Pressure
stories.blurb: The Trump administration is pressuring Walmart and other major grocery chains over rising food prices, particularly beef, while expanding a Justice Department price-fixing probe into the industry.

stories.name: Walmart delivery expansion
stories.blurb: Walmart is expanding its delivery business by partnering with restaurant chains like Dunkin' and Papa Johns and testing drone delivery, directly challenging services like DoorDash and Uber Eats.

stories.name: Walmart Valuation Debate
stories.blurb: Analysts and investors are debating whether Walmart's stock, despite strong sales growth, is overvalued and worth buying ahead of and after its latest earnings report.

past.name: Grocery Industry Shakeup
past.blurb: A wave of store closures and shifting consumer habits is putting pressure on major grocery chains like Kroger, Dollar General, and other discount grocers as they scramble to adapt and compete.

8.text: Costco posted a fifth straight earnings beat with 10.7% U.S. comparable sales growth and strong inventory turnover, leading analysts to call it a better buy than Walmart, whose revenue growth is slowing. Walmart appears only as a comparison point, with Costco favored operationally and in dividend and valuation analyses.

9.text: Target cut prices on 2,000+ items; a 101-year-old chain closed 27 stores; Walmart, Aldi, and Kroger matched Costco; Walmart recalled two lots of a store-brand frozen meal over listeria; Halloween spending is set to hit a record.

7.text: Walmart is expanding delivery, gas discounts, holiday offerings, and a new Texas store, while scaling retail media and testing Flipkart purchases through Google Gemini in India. CEO John Furner pledged Walmart won't use personal data or AI to set individualized prices as digital shelf labels roll out.

5.text: Walmart drew multiple downgrades over valuation concerns, with analysts citing its rich P/E, margin pressure, and weaker consumers despite growth in grocery, e-commerce, and advertising. Shares fell 1.78% to $106.80; Mizuho cut its price target to $125 while keeping Outperform.

4.text: A Fed study found only 15% of firms plan to pass tariff refunds to consumers, with Walmart among them, as Customs has collected $166 billion in tariffs. Separately, Trump officials are weighing rolling back a beef import plan amid GOP midterm concerns.

6.text: ALDI is expanding its ready-to-eat meal offerings to compete with Walmart and Kroger for shoppers seeking cheaper, faster dinners. The move intensifies competition in the grocery sector, though Walmart is mentioned only as a rival being targeted.
